eyebrow: Python for Data Science · Chapter 1, Lesson 4
subtitle: Give a repeated operation a name — reuse it, test it, read it.

caption: rate=0.08 is a default value — naming an argument (rate=0.10) makes a call easier to read.
Python packs multiple return values into a tuple you unpack on the spot.

code:
def no_return(x):
    x * 2

result = no_return(3)
print(result)   # None
caption: The doubled value gets computed, then thrown away — a function with no return hands back None.

code:
totals = [20.0, 55.5, 130.0, 8.25]
with_tax = [add_tax(t) for t in totals]
# [21.6, 59.94, 140.4, 8.91]

big = [t for t in totals if t > 20]
# [55.5, 130.0]
caption: [expression for item in items if condition] — an if at the end filters items out.
An if...else at the front transforms every item; {key: value for ...} builds a dict.

code:
orders = [("Ada", 55.5), ("Grace", 8.25), ("Linus", 130.0)]
print(sorted(orders, key=lambda o: o[1], reverse=True))
# [('Linus', 130.0), ('Ada', 55.5), ('Grace', 8.25)]
caption: Most useful as a key argument when sorting — you'll meet this pattern again in pandas.
